why: In NEH 12:36 'וְאֶחָיו' means Zechariah's fellow musicians, not siblings, so the text does not plainly make Hanani his brother.
'אֵשֶׁת הוֹדִיָּה' is 'the wife of Hodiah', so Hodiah (recorded as male) is the husband; nothing in the text makes Hodiah Eshtemoa's mother.
'וּבָנָיו אוּלָם וָרָקֶם' in 1CH 7:16 could refer to Peresh or to Sheresh, and the text does not decide which.
The Salma of 1CH 2:11 is Salmon, and 'boaz son-of salmon' is already recorded; the salma record is a different man, Hur's son (1CH 2:51).
1CH 5:14 does say 'בֶּן־גִּלְעָד בֶּן־מִיכָאֵל', so Gilead is the son of Michael; the record's mixing of two Michaels is a separate problem.
NEH 11:15 does say 'Azrikam son of Hashabiah'; if hashabiah-2 (Jeduthun's son) is the wrong man, the row should be repointed, not removed.
The Masoretic text of EZR 8:5 reads only 'of the sons of Shecaniah, son of Jahaziel'; Zattu comes from the LXX/1 Esdras, not this chapter.
The Hebrew 'אֲבִי עֵיטָם' makes Jezreel and the others belong to 'the father of Etam' (Etam is a town), not sons of a person Etam.
1CH 4:2 says 'Reaiah son of Shobal', and Hur's son Shobal (1CH 2:50-53, with Haroeh and the Zorathites) is the right man.
1CH 1:32 says 'קְטוּרָה פִּילֶגֶשׁ אַבְרָהָם', abram is the Abraham record, and nothing between them is recorded yet.
'אֲחוֹת נַחַם אֲבִי קְעִילָה' can make Naham the father of Keilah or make 'the father of Keilah' a son of Hodiah's wife alongside Eshtemoa; the text does not settle it.
The houses in NEH 12:12-21 match the priests who went up with Zerubbabel in 12:1-7, so 'of Amariah' means that Amariah, not the signer of NEH 10.
Mash/Meshech is listed among the 'sons of Shem' in the broad sense; 'mash descendant-of shem' and 'aram father-of mash' already record it correctly.
EZR 7:1 does say Seraiah son of Azariah son of Hilkiah, which matches 1CH 6:13-14, so seraiah-2 and azariah-7 are the right people.
'וְאֶחָיו לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָיו' means clan kinsmen by their families, not that Jeiel was Beerah's sibling.
The Salma of 1CH 2:11 is Salmon, already recorded as Nahshon's son; the salma record is Hur's son, a different man.
Whether 'וְאַחְיוֹ שָׁשָׁק' (8:14) belongs to the 'sons of Beriah' of 8:16, or names his brothers, is disputed, and Shashak has his own sons in 8:22-25.
In the David-era clan list of 1CH 23:18, 'sons of Izhar' means descendants (Izhar's sons are Korah, Nepheg and Zichri), and 'descendant-of' is already recorded.
GEN 4:22 names Naamah inside Zillah's sentence as Tubal-cain's sister but does not say Zillah bore her, so she could be a half-sister through Lamech.
1CH 5:14 'אֵלֶּה בְּנֵי אֲבִיחַיִל' makes the seven of 5:13, Meshullam and Zia among them, sons of Abihail and so brothers.
Nahath is Reuel's son (GEN 36:13), so he is Basemath's grandson; 'sons of Basemath' supports descendant-of, not son-of.
NEH 12:1 does say Jeremiah went up with Zerubbabel, so the claim that the chapter does not say it is false; whether jeremiah-7 is the right person is a separate question.
MT 'אֲבִי עֵיטָם' does not make a person Etam the father of Ishma; Etam is a place and 'father of Etam' is its founder.
NEH 12:35 does say 'Mattaniah son of Micaiah'; if mattaniah-4 (2CH 29:13) is the wrong man, the row should be repointed, not removed.
'אֵשֶׁת הוֹדִיָּה' makes Hodiah (recorded as male) the husband, and Keilah is at most a grandson, so 'mother-of' has no support.
The chain in EZR 7:1-2 (Azariah, Hilkiah, Shallum, Zadok, Ahitub) is the high-priestly line of 1CH 6:13-14, so seraiah-2 is the right Seraiah and seraiah-11 looks like a duplicate.
The eliel record is a Manassite clan head (1CH 5:24), not Samuel's ancestor; that ancestor is already recorded as 'elihu father-of jeroham'.
The jediael record is David's warrior, son of Shimri (1CH 11:45), not the Benjamite of 1CH 7:6.
'naaman descendant-of benjamin' (GEN 46:21) and 'naaman son-of bela-2' (NUM 26:40) are already recorded, and son-of would contradict them.
1CH 2:16 'ואחיתיהם צְרוּיָה וַאֲבִיגָיִל' names Abigail as the sister of Jesse's sons listed in 2:13-15, Ozem among them, and nothing between them is recorded.
NUM 3:35 makes Zuriel the prince of the families of Merari (the clan), not commander of Merari the son of Levi, who is the record named.
'וְאֶחָיו' in NEH 12:36 means Zechariah's fellow musicians; nothing makes Maai and Milalai siblings of each other.
'Of Meraioth' in NEH 12:15 is the priestly house of 12:3 (Meremoth), not Meraioth son of Ahitub (1CH 9:11).
In NEH 12:36 'וְאֶחָיו' means fellow musicians, not siblings, so the text does not make Nethanel Zechariah's brother.
1CH 4:1 is a line of descent and Shobal is Hur's son (1CH 2:50-53, Haroeh and the Zorathites), so shobal-2 is correct and shobal-3 is a self-described possible duplicate.
1CH 5:14 'אֵלֶּה בְּנֵי אֲבִיחַיִל' refers to the seven of 5:13, Meshullam among them.
Mahli is Levi's grandson through Merari, 'בֶּן־לֵוִי' here means descendant, and 'mahli descendant-of levi' is already recorded.
michael-2 is recorded as son of Jeshishai and father of Gilead, Abihail's ancestor (1CH 5:14), so making him Abihail's son creates a loop; the record mixes two Michaels.
MT 'אֲבִי עֵיטָם' does not make Ishma the son of a person Etam; Etam is a town whose 'father' is named.
NEH 12:1 does say these priests went up with Jeshua, so the claim that the chapter does not say it is false.
'וְאָחִיו אָסָף' calls Asaph Heman's fellow Levite singer: Heman is a Kohathite (6:33-38) and Asaph a Gershonite (6:39-43), so they are not siblings.
'Of Iddo' in NEH 12:16 is the priestly house of the Iddo who went up with Zerubbabel (12:4), which is iddo-7, not the prophet's grandfather of EZR 5:1.
'וְאֶחָיו לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָיו' means kinsmen by clans, not that Zechariah was Beerah's sibling.
'יְכָנְיָה בְנוֹ צִדְקִיָּה בְנוֹ' under the heading 'sons of Jehoiakim' can mean two sons of Jehoiakim or a chain making Zedekiah Jeconiah's son; the text does not decide.
1CH 7:13 calls Naphtali's sons, Jahziel among them, 'בְּנֵי בִלְהָה', and no direct row between Jahzeel and Bilhah exists yet.
1CH 2:16 names Abigail as the sister of Jesse's sons in 2:13-15, Abinadab among them, and nothing between them is recorded.
'וּבָנָיו' in 1CH 7:16 could be Peresh's sons or Sheresh's sons; the text does not decide.
1CH 2:16 names Abigail as the sister of Jesse's sons in 2:13-15, Eliab among them, and no sibling row between them exists.
EZR 7:1 does say 'עֶזְרָא בֶּן־שְׂרָיָה'; since Seraiah died in 586 the link is ancestry, which calls for retyping, not removal.
'וּבָנָיו אוּלָם וָרָקֶם' could be Peresh's sons or Sheresh's sons; the text does not decide.
